newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOTOR RACING-HILL NEGOTIATES SPEEDY INTERVIEWS.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-HILL NEGOTIATES SPEEDY INTERVIEWS.

text.p: New Formula One world champion Damon Hill sped through hours of press interviews on Monday, negotiating slippery questions about his future with the same skill he showed in winning the title.
Hill refused to rise to baited questions about whether in his moment of glory he felt bitter about his rejection by the Williams team as its driver next season when he had won them a world title.

He spent more than four hours in the Reuter Television studio in Tokyo answering almost non-stop questions from more than a dozen mainly British news organisations in live radio and television broadcasts.
"I feel no bitterness towards Williams. It was their decision. I didn't want to go but they thought it was for the best and that's life," Hill said. "I'm moving on and that's the end of the story."
"I wish them well and am glad I could leave them on the right note in winning my last race for them," he added.

The 36-year-old Briton wrapped up the title on Sunday when he won the Japan Grand Prix at Suzuka. His nearest rival Jacques Villeneuve, also driving a Williams, lost his chance of glory when he retired with 15 laps to go.
Hill said he went into the race determined to take the lead from the start to take the pressure off himself and put it on Villeneuve.
"I concentrated extra hard on the start and it paid off," Hill said.
Hill said his concentration faltered for several laps when he learned Villeneuve had pulled out, effectively handing him the title.
"I had to pull myself back together and then I focused on winning the race and not letting up," Hill said.
Hill said the world title, following those of his father Graham in 1962 and 1968, was a dream moment and he felt like celebrating until Christmas.
"Nothing has stopped since I got out of the car at Suzuka," he said.
Looking into the future, Williams said his new team TWR Arrows had the potential to win some races next year but he stopped short of forecasting another world title for himself.
"It won't be easy to defend the title," he said. "We have a lot of hard work to do but I'm excited about the challenge and looking forward to it."
